craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as Lordhood (viśveśvaratva); bhakti as worship; vyabhicāri wonder at all-opposites mirrored. Sanskrit-first: bhaja mood open per UNC (worship kept as act, mood unforced); compounds open kept (own-grasping-consciousness-rise carried whole — density IS the metaphysics). Abhinavagupta frame: mirror (darpaṇa) as the accurate instrument — opposites shine WITHOUT entering; knowing = glory = Lordhood (equation, not ascent). Rows: 9 (true/untrue, little/much, lasting/lasting-not, Māyā-stained/self-pure — all pairs kept; trimming would un-mirror the mirror), 1 (‘lordship of all’ closes — viśveśvaratva last, the equation's answer), 12 (śānta-fall: ‘three-’ … ‘all’ — whole-work close, wide and still). Close: ‘worship lordship of all’. Rupture: ‘know it:’ (all-shown turns to all-known — colon stages the equation). Rejected: trimming pairs — killed: all-pairs IS the mirror; resolving bhaja — killed by UNC; ‘serve the Lord of all’ — killed: bhaja + aiśvarya is worship-lordship, service weakens. Read aloud: WHAT is TRUE, WHAT un-TRUE … ALL-shines IN the MIR-ror OF-con-SCIOUS-ness … KNOW-it: GLO-ry MOUNT-ed ON your OWN ex-PER-i-ence — WOR-ship LORD-ship OF-all.

lines: What is true, what untrue, little or much, lasting or lasting-not, Māyā-stained or self-pure — all shines in the mirror of consciousness.
All that — risen from self-grasping consciousness, natured as form and light — know it: glory mounted on your own experience — worship lordship of all.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yat satyaṃ yad asatyam alpabahulaṃ nityaṃ na nityaṃ ca yat yan māyāmalinaṃ yad ātmavimalaṃ ciddarpaṇe rājate | tat sarvaṃ svavimarśasaṃvidudayād rūpaprakāśātmakaṃ jñātvā svānubhavādhirūḍhamahimā viśveśvaratvaṃ bhaja

reads_against.argmap: What shines in the mirror, and what follows from knowing it? → All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror; knowing that all is own-grasping-consciousness-rise = glory = Lordhood; worship.
c1_essence: All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror: true/untrue, little/much, eternal/non-eternal, Māyā-stained/self-pure. That all, from own-grasping-consciousness-rise, form-light-natured, having known — own-experience-risen glory: Lordhood — worship. Knowing that all opposites shine in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness = glory = Lordhood; its last word is the imperative it opened with the stance for.
